questions.prompt: Which triangle has three equal sides?
options: Isosceles with exactly two equal sides
questions.explanation: Equilateral means all three sides are equal.

questions.prompt: Which property must every rectangle have?
options: Exactly one pair of parallel sides
questions.explanation: Every rectangle has four right angles; equal adjacent sides are not required.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a square is correct?
options: It is neither a rectangle nor a rhombus.
It is a rectangle but never a rhombus.
It is both a rectangle and a rhombus.
It is a rhombus but never a rectangle.
questions.explanation: A square has four right angles and four equal sides.

questions.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a non-square rectangle have?
questions.explanation: Its two symmetry lines pass through the midpoints of opposite sides.

questions.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
questions.explanation: Each vertex-to-opposite-midpoint line is a symmetry line.

questions.prompt: Which property describes a parallelogram?
options: Exactly one pair of sides is parallel.
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
questions.explanation: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel opposite sides.

questions.prompt: In this course, a trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides. Which shape meets that definition?
options: A quadrilateral with one parallel pair and one non-parallel pair
questions.explanation: This uses the stated exclusive definition; conventions can differ between textbooks.

questions.prompt: A triangle has two equal sides. What can you conclude about the opposite angles?
questions.explanation: Equal sides in a triangle have equal opposite angles.

questions.prompt: Which statement must be true for a rhombus?
options: All four angles are right angles.
It has exactly one parallel pair.
questions.explanation: A rhombus has equal sides, but need not have right angles.

questions.prompt: Which property describes a kite?
options: Two pairs of adjacent equal sides
Exactly one pair of equal opposite sides
questions.explanation: The equal sides in a kite meet at adjacent vertices.

questions.prompt: What is the interior-angle sum of a 3-sided convex polygon, in degrees?
What is the interior-angle sum of a 4-sided convex polygon, in degrees?
What is the interior-angle sum of a 5-sided convex polygon, in degrees?
What is the interior-angle sum of a 6-sided convex polygon, in degrees?
What is each interior angle of a regular 5-sided polygon, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Divide the sum 540° by 5.

questions.prompt: What is each interior angle of a regular 6-sided polygon, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Divide the sum 720° by 6.

questions.prompt: What is each interior angle of a regular 8-sided polygon, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Divide the sum 1080° by 8.

questions.prompt: A regular polygon has exterior angles of 30°. How many sides does it have?
A convex polygon has interior-angle sum 1260°. How many sides does it have?
Can a regular polygon have exterior angles of 50°?
options: No, because 360 ÷ 50 is not a whole number.
questions.explanation: The number of equal exterior angles must be a positive whole number; 7.2 sides is impossible.

questions.prompt: Two angles on a straight line are 67° and x. What is x in degrees?
Angles at a point are 80°, 110°, 95° and x. What is x in degrees?
Two lines intersect. An angle is 48°. What is its vertically opposite angle in degrees?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal.

questions.prompt: Parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. An angle is 72°. What is its corresponding angle in degrees?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles between parallel lines are equal.

questions.prompt: Parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. An angle is 115°. What is its alternate interior angle in degrees?
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles between parallel lines are equal.

questions.prompt: Two co-interior angles between parallel lines are 124° and x. What is x in degrees?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles add to 180°, so x = 56.

questions.prompt: A triangle has angles 35° and 65°. What is its third angle in degrees?
An isosceles triangle has vertex angle 40°. What is either base angle in degrees?
questions.explanation: The two equal base angles share 140°: 140 ÷ 2 = 70.

questions.prompt: A quadrilateral has angles 90°, 75°, 110° and x. What is x in degrees?
When do corresponding angles have to be equal?
options: Whenever any two lines are crossed.
When the two lines crossed by the transversal are parallel.
Only when the transversal is vertical.
Only when the angles are acute.
questions.explanation: Parallelism is the condition that guarantees corresponding-angle equality.

questions.prompt: What does a perpendicular bisector do to a segment?
options: It is parallel to the segment.
It passes through the midpoint at 90°.
It passes through an endpoint at 45°.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular specifies 90°; bisector specifies the midpoint.

questions.prompt: To construct the perpendicular bisector of AB, how should the two compass radii compare?
options: One must be twice the other.
questions.explanation: Equal radii make the arc intersections equidistant from A and B.

questions.prompt: For a perpendicular-bisector construction, the compass radius must be…
questions.explanation: The arcs need two intersections, one on each side of the segment.

questions.prompt: What should be joined after the two equal-radius arc pairs intersect?
options: The two endpoints of the original segment again
An endpoint to the other endpoint’s arc centre
Any two points on one arc
questions.explanation: Joining the intersections produces the perpendicular bisector.

questions.prompt: Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is…
options: twice as far from A as B.
equally distant from A and B.
questions.explanation: Equal distance from the endpoints characterises the perpendicular bisector.

questions.prompt: What does an angle bisector create?
options: Two right angles in every case
Two angles adding to 90° in every case
questions.explanation: An angle bisector halves the original angle.

questions.prompt: Which tools perform a standard compass-and-straightedge bisector construction?
questions.explanation: The arcs establish equal distances and the straightedge joins the required points.

questions.prompt: In an angle-bisector construction, why draw matching arcs from the two points on the arms?
options: To measure the original angle in degrees
To find a point equally distant from those two points
To make the two arms parallel
questions.explanation: Together with the first equal-radius arc, this gives congruent triangles.

questions.prompt: Is measuring half an angle with a protractor the same method as a compass-and-straightedge construction?
options: Yes; arcs are unnecessary in a compass construction.
No; the compass construction uses equal-distance arcs.
No; angle bisection is impossible without a protractor.
questions.explanation: The construction should be justified by equal distances, not a measured approximation.

questions.prompt: Why must you keep the same compass opening for paired arcs?
options: To make the picture more colourful
To preserve the equal distances needed by the construction
questions.explanation: Changing the radius breaks the equal-distance argument.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 8 cm by 5 cm. What is its area in cm²?
A rectangle is 8 cm by 5 cm. What is its perimeter in cm?
A triangle has base 10 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. What is its area in cm²?
A parallelogram has base 7 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm. What is its area in cm²?
questions.explanation: Base × perpendicular height = 7 × 4 = 28.

questions.prompt: A square has side length 3.5 cm. What is its perimeter in cm?
A rectangle has area 36 cm² and width 4 cm. What is its length in cm?
questions.explanation: Length = area ÷ width = 36 ÷ 4.

questions.prompt: A triangle has area 24 cm² and base 8 cm. What is its perpendicular height in cm?
questions.explanation: Height = 2 × area ÷ base = 48 ÷ 8.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 4.5 cm by 2 cm. What is its area in cm²?
A square has area 49 cm². What is its perimeter in cm?
questions.explanation: Side = 7 cm; perimeter = 4 × 7 = 28 cm.

questions.prompt: Which unit is appropriate for area?
questions.explanation: Area measures two-dimensional coverage, so square units are needed.

questions.prompt: A 10 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a 4 cm by 3 cm corner removed. What is the remaining area in cm²?
A 9 cm by 7 cm rectangle has a 3 cm by 2 cm corner removed. What is the remaining area in cm²?
A 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a 5 cm by 4 cm corner removed. What is the remaining area in cm²?
A 10 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a 4 cm by 3 cm corner notch removed. What is the L-shape perimeter in cm?
questions.explanation: Removing a rectangular corner replaces two boundary lengths with equal inward lengths; total = 2(width + height).

questions.prompt: A 12 cm by 9 cm rectangle has a 5 cm by 2 cm corner notch removed. What is the L-shape perimeter in cm?
questions.explanation: Removing a rectangular corner replaces two boundary lengths with equal inward lengths; total = 2(width + height).

questions.prompt: Three rectangles have non-overlapping interiors and areas 12 cm², 15 cm² and 8 cm². What is their combined area in cm²?
questions.explanation: Add the three non-overlapping areas: 12 + 15 + 8 = 35.

questions.prompt: A compound region consists of three non-overlapping rectangles: 4 cm by 3 cm, 2 cm by 5 cm and 3 cm by 2 cm. What is the total area in cm²?
A 6.5 cm by 4 cm rectangle has a 1.5 cm by 2 cm corner removed. What is the remaining area in cm²?
Two 3 cm by 2 cm rectangles are joined along a complete 2 cm side without overlap. What is the perimeter of the combined shape in cm?
questions.explanation: Each perimeter is 10 cm, but the shared 2 cm edge is internal and counted twice: 20 − 4 = 16 cm.

questions.prompt: Why can adding the separate rectangle perimeters give a wrong compound-shape perimeter?
options: A compound shape has no perimeter.
Shared internal edges are not on the outer boundary.
questions.explanation: Trace only the boundary, or subtract twice every shared edge.
